subject: Difference between plyr and dplyr in running a function on grouped data (not a data frame?)

messages.author: 5a3ca9144379802e
messages.subject: Difference between plyr and dplyr in running a function on grouped data (not a data frame?)
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to run a function on a rather large data frame, grouped by a variable named "npat.id". In particular, I am trying to get the mode of every single variable organized by group. That is, I'm trying to reduce "subsets" of data frames with indeterminate numbers of rows to a single row, then reassemble the whole thing into a new data frame.

Here's reproducible code using plyr that works fine:

df = data.frame(npat.id = c(35,35,35,94,94,94), first = c("Mark","Mark","Mark","Ellen","Ellen","Ellen"), q16 = c(NA,1,1,0,NA,0), q33 = c(NA,0,0,0,1,0))

> df
  npat.id first q16 q33
1      35  Mark  NA  NA
2      35  Mark   1   0
3      35  Mark   1   0
4      94 Ellen   0   0
5      94 Ellen  NA   1
6      94 Ellen   0   0
> 

# below from http://stackoverflow.com/questions/2547402/standard-library-function-in-r-for-finding-the-mode
 Mode <- function(x, na.rm=T) {
    ux <- unique(x)
    if (na.rm) { ux = na.omit(ux)[1]}
    ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
  }

  colmode <- function(x) { mode.result <- apply(x,2,Mode) }

  system.time(output.df <- ddply(df,.(npat.id),colmode,.progress="text"))

> output.df
  npat.id first q16 q33
1      35  Mark   1   0
2      94 Ellen   0   0

As you can see, the original data frame with four rows and two groups gets reduced to a single row per group correctly. NAs are thrown out. I use the Mode() function I got from Stack Overflow because it works with any type of variable: numeric, character, etc.

This solution works, but for my large data frame it takes a long time. So I was interested to try Hadley's new dplyr (I am running version 0.2 on R 3.1.0 on Windows 7 64 bit). My best effort, however, fails:

output.df <-
  df %.%
  group_by(npat.id) %.%
  do(colmode(.))

I get the error that "Results are not data frames at positions: 1, 2". Which doesn't quite make sense to me.

Thank you in advance for any ideas; I'm sure its something obvious but I can't quite figure it out.

Boris Shor

messages.subject: Re: Difference between plyr and dplyr in running a function on grouped data (not a data frame?)
parts:
There are a couple things to fix... first, the Mode function doesn't actually return the mode when na.rm=T:

library(plyr)
library(dplyr)

df <- data.frame(npat.id = c(35,35,35,94,94,94), first = c("Mark","Mark","Mark","Ellen","Ellen","Ellen"), q16 = c(NA,1,1,0,NA,0), q33 = c(NA,0,0,0,1,0))

Mode <- function(x, na.rm=T) {
  ux <- unique(x)
  if (na.rm) { ux = na.omit(ux)[1]}
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}

Mode(c(1,2,3,3,4))
# 1

Also, the colmode function returns a named character vector, but dplyr::do needs a data frame:

str(colmode(df))
# Named chr [1:4] "35" "Mark" " 1" " 0"
# - attr(*, "names")= chr [1:4] "npat.id" "first" "q16" "q33"



Here are fixed versions:

Mode <- function(x, na.rm=T) {
  ux <- unique(x)
  if (na.rm) {

ux <- ux[!is.na(ux)]
  }
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}
Mode(c(1,2,3,3,4))
# 3

colmodes <- function(x) { colwise(Mode)(x) }
str(colmodes(df))
# 'data.frame':  1 obs. of  4 variables:
#  $ npat.id: num 35
#  $ first  : Factor w/ 2 levels "Ellen","Mark": 2
#  $ q16    : num 1
#  $ q33    : num 0

df %>%
  group_by(npat.id) %>%
  do(colmodes(.))
# Source: local data frame [2 x 4]
# Groups: npat.id
# 
#   npat.id first q16 q33
# 1      35  Mark   1   0
# 2      94 Ellen   0   0


-Winston
